en: The Legend of the Elder Sudassana Sobhita Chapter, Number Two [Verse 1] I was a king named Sudassana, ruling over the earth with its seven islands. At that time, the Teacher, the Buddha, appeared in the world. [Verse 2] The Teacher, the Blessed One, the Great Sage, went forth into homelessness. He attained supreme enlightenment at the foot of the Bodhi tree. [Verse 3] Having become enlightened, the Teacher, the Blessed One, set out for Benares. There he turned the Wheel of Dhamma, which had never been turned before by anyone in the world. [Verse 4] When the Teacher, the Blessed One, had turned the Wheel of Dhamma, I heard the teaching of the Dhamma from the mouth of the Conqueror. [Verse 5] Hearing the Dhamma, I took refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha. I became a lay follower, undertaking the five precepts. [Verse 6] Having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, I gave alms-food to the Teacher. I offered a bowl filled with various kinds of food. [Verse 7] Having given that alms-food to the Teacher, I made this aspiration: "May I, through this root of merit, attain the state of a Buddha. [Verse 8] Through that root of merit, I have wandered through many hundreds of thousands of eons. For eighty-four thousand eons, I never fell into the lower realms. [Verse 9] In every birth, I was reborn as a human being. I was always a king, a lord of the earth, possessing great power. [Verse 10] Now, having fulfilled my perfections, I have attained supreme enlightenment. I am the Teacher, the Blessed One, the Great Sage, who has crossed over the flood. [Verse 11] I have taught the Dhamma that leads to liberation; I have shown the path that leads to the cessation of suffering. [Verse 12] Those who have heard my teaching and practiced it accordingly, Have all crossed over the great ocean of saṃsāra. [Verse 13] This is the legacy of the Elder Sudassana; Having heard it, one should practice with diligence. By doing so, one will reach the end of suffering. Thus spoke the Elder Sudassana. [Verse 14] The Elder Sudassana, having completed his life-span, Passed away and was reborn in the Brahmā world. From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Tusita heaven. From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Nimmānarati heaven. [Verse 15] From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven. From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Suddhāvāsa Brahmā world. From there, he passed away and was reborn in the human world. From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven. [Verse 16] From there, he passed away and was reborn in the Yāma heaven. “On the bank of the Vinatā River,
a pilakkhu tree was in fruit;
searching for that tree, I— ”
I saw the Leader of the World.
Having seen a ketaka flower in bloom,
I then cut it from its stalk.
I offered it to the Buddha Sikhin,
the kinsman of the world—
by means of that knowledge which you have attained, [may I too attain it].
The deathless, the immortal state—
I revere that knowledge,
O Best of Buddhas, Great Sage.
Having performed an offering to Knowledge,
I saw a Pilakkhu tree;
I have attained that wisdom.
This is the fruit of the offering of knowledge.
Because I offered that flower thirty-one eons ago,
I do not recall being born in an evil state;
this is the fruit of honoring with knowledge.
Thirteen aeons from now,
Twelve were born with their teeth already emerged;
they were universal monarchs, endowed with the seven treasures and of great fruit.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Sudassana spoke these verses.
This is the second *apadāna* of the elder Sudassana.
